does: Stirs honey and cinnamon into the sauce of a tagine once the meat is tender, and boils it down in the open pot until the onions melt into a dark, sticky, sweet sauce that coats the meat, the way of a Moroccan mʿassel.
how: Lift the meat out first if the pot is crowded, so that the sauce can boil freely.
Stir in the honey and the cinnamon with any fruit.
Boil gently with the lid off, stirring and scraping the bottom, as the sauce thickens.
Stop when the sauce is dark and glossy and holds a line drawn across the pot with a spoon.
Put the meat back and turn it in the sauce.

cues.text: A dark, shiny sauce that holds a track drawn with a spoon.
Warm honey and cinnamon. A bitter burnt sugar smell means it has caught.

mistakes.mistake: Boiling too hard at the end, so that the honey catches on the bottom and burns.
mistakes.fix: Lower the heat as the sauce thickens and scrape the bottom often.

mistakes.mistake: Adding the honey at the start, so that it burns or turns flat during the long cooking.
mistakes.fix: Add it only once the meat is tender.

variant_of.differs: Honey and cinnamon are stirred in and the sauce is boiled down until sticky and nearly caramel, not only until it is stronger.
